messages.author: 1f723d378f24adbb
messages.subject: how to debug vanishing density?
parts:
Hi,

I ran into a "vanishing density" problem at initialization. After
eyeballing the model, it turned out it was misspecified (one variable
which ostensibly had a lognormal distribution assumed a 0 value for some
of the data).

But it took a lot of time to find the problem, mainly by print
statements of left- and right hand sides. I was wondering if there is a
quicker way of doing this, so I thought I would print lp__ before and
after each statement and then I would notice if it gets to a nonsensical
value.

However, it always printed the same (!) value for me, and stan of course
warned me that lp__ is deprecated (I am using 2.4). So I am wondering
how to do what I originally wanted the "right" way --- is there a way to
print the lp__ increment for each sampling statement?

Best,

Tamas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] [Cmd/Py/R-Stan] how to debug vanishing density?
parts:
D'oh! It just dawned on me what the problem is. For efficiency,
the log prob increment statements add to an accumulator and then
apply sum() at the end, rather than incrementing lp__ directly.
The increment is only at the very end, after all the model statements
get called. Until then, you're seeing only the Jacobian from constrained
variables all the way through.

I'm going to add a log_prob() function with no-args ASAP
that will go through the accumulator and print the sum. Then that
will be the recommended function for debugging lp():

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/470

The other thing we need to do is not swallow the warning messages.
Right now, initialization swallows the warning message then tries again.
Those should print. I re-opened the issue which had been prematurely
closed (or perhaps it moved --- I can't find the new target, so I reopened
this one):

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/779

The big goal, which isn't going to happen right away, is to get
line numbers into the error reports. We know how to do it, but it's
going to be a fair bit of work.

I'll get the first one done for Stan 2.5 and the second done for
CmdStan, but then the same behavior needs to be replicated in PyStan
and RStan.

- Bob
